;;; $801E: Level load: init buffers, background, start screens ;;;
;; Three routines. $05801E (JSL from game mode level load): fills the layer 2 background buffer
;;     $7EB900-$7EC0FF, decompresses a
;; prebuilt background if the layer 2 bank byte [$6A] is $FF, clears the Map16 buffers ($7EC800 = $25, $7FC800
;;     = 0), runs LoadLevel
;; and (game mode < $22) calls $A751.
;; $05809E: draws the first 32 columns/rows of layers 1 and 2 around the scroll position (calling the column
;;     builders and the VRAM DMA),
;; cycles the pointers of Map16 tiles $133-$13A, and sets TM/TS and window masks from [$0D9D]/[$0D9E].
;; $058126: decompresses RLE data at [$68] to $7E:B900 (control byte: bit 7 = repeat next byte, low 7 bits =
;;     count - 1; $FFFF ends).
;; Called by:
;;     $00:95CE: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9716: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode)
$05:801E 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$05:801F E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8021 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; X and Y 16-bit
$05:8023 A2 00 00     LDX.W #$0000                    ; \
$05:8026 A9 25        LDA.B #$25                      ; |
$05:8028 9F 00 B9 7E  STA.L $7EB900,X                 ; |
$05:802C 9F 00 BB 7E  STA.L $7EBB00,X                 ; } Fill $7EB900-$7EBCFF (layer 2 background tile low bytes) with $25 (blank tile)
$05:8030 E8           INX                             ; |
$05:8031 E0 00 02     CPX.W #$0200                    ; |
$05:8034 D0 F0        BNE $8026                       ; / Repeat for X = 0..$1FF
$05:8036 9C 28 19     STZ.W $1928                     ; [$1928] = 0 (screen counter used while loading level data)
$05:8039 A5 6A        LDA $6A                         ; \
$05:803B C9 FF        CMP.B #$FF                      ; |
$05:803D D0 35        BNE $8074                       ; / Layer 2 bank [$6A] = $FF means a prebuilt background; otherwise skip to $8074
$05:803F C2 10        REP #$10                        ; X and Y 16-bit
$05:8041 A0 00 00     LDY.W #$0000                    ; \
$05:8044 A6 68        LDX $68                         ; |
$05:8046 E0 FE E8     CPX.W #$E8FE                    ; } Y = background Map16 page: 0, or 1 if layer 2 pointer [$68] >= $E8FE
$05:8049 90 03        BCC $804E                       ; |
$05:804B A0 01 00     LDY.W #$0001                    ; /
$05:804E A2 00 00     LDX.W #$0000                    ; \
$05:8051 98           TYA                             ; |
$05:8052 9F 00 BD 7E  STA.L $7EBD00,X                 ; } Store Y (Map16 page) as every background tile's high byte
$05:8056 9F 00 BF 7E  STA.L $7EBF00,X                 ; |
$05:805A E8           INX                             ; |
$05:805B E0 00 02     CPX.W #$0200                    ; |
$05:805E D0 F2        BNE $8052                       ; /
$05:8060 A9 0C        LDA.B #$0C                      ; \
$05:8062 85 6A        STA $6A                         ; / Layer 2 bank = $0C (all prebuilt backgrounds live in bank $0C)
$05:8064 9C 32 19     STZ.W $1932                     ; \
$05:8067 9C 31 19     STZ.W $1931                     ; / Tileset [$1931] and [$1932] = 0
$05:806A A2 00 B9     LDX.W #$B900                    ; \
$05:806D 86 0D        STX $0D                         ; / [$0D] = $B900: destination of the background data ([$0F] = $7E is set by the callee)
$05:806F C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8071 20 26 81     JSR.W $8126                     ; Decompress the layer 2 background at [$68] into $7E:B900
$05:8074 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8076 A2 00 00     LDX.W #$0000                    ; X = 0
$05:8079 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; A = 0
$05:807B 20 3A 83     JSR.W $833A                     ; Clear $7FC800-$7FFFFF (Map16 high bytes), X-th byte of each 512-byte page; X++
$05:807E CA           DEX                             ; X-- (undo the INX so both fills use the same X)
$05:807F A9 25        LDA.B #$25                      ; A = $25 (blank tile)
$05:8081 20 C8 82     JSR.W $82C8                     ; Fill $7EC800-$7EFFFF (Map16 low bytes) with $25 the same way; X++
$05:8084 E0 00 02     CPX.W #$0200                    ; \
$05:8087 D0 F0        BNE $8079                       ; / Repeat for X = 0..$1FF (whole $3800-byte buffers)
$05:8089 9C 28 19     STZ.W $1928                     ; [$1928] = 0
$05:808C 20 AC 83     JSR.W LoadLevel                 ; Load the level objects of both layers (LoadLevel)
$05:808F E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:8091 AD 00 01     LDA.W RAM_GameMode              ; \
$05:8094 C9 22        CMP.B #$22                      ; |
$05:8096 10 04        BPL $809C                       ; / If game mode < $22, run $A751 (probably spawns the initial sprites)
$05:8098 22 51 A7 02  JSL.L $A751                     ; Run $A751 (probably the initial sprite load)
$05:809C 28           PLP                             ; Restore processor flags
$05:809D 6B           RTL                             ; Return

$05:809E 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$05:809F E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:80A1 9C 28 19     STZ.W $1928                     ; [$1928] = 0 (column counter)
$05:80A4 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$05:80A6 A9 FF FF     LDA.W #$FFFF                    ; \
$05:80A9 85 4D        STA $4D                         ; |
$05:80AB 85 4F        STA $4F                         ; / [$4D]-[$50] = $FFFF (probably 'nothing drawn yet' markers)
$05:80AD 20 7E 87     JSR.W $877E                     ; Compute the visible area's edge positions from the scroll into [$45]-[$4B] ($877E)
$05:80B0 A5 45        LDA $45                         ; \
$05:80B2 85 47        STA $47                         ; / [$47] = [$45] (start at the left/first edge)
$05:80B4 A5 49        LDA $49                         ; \
$05:80B6 85 4B        STA $4B                         ; / [$4B] = [$49] (start at the top/first edge)
$05:80B8 A9 02 02     LDA.W #$0202                    ; \
$05:80BB 85 55        STA $55                         ; / [$55] = $0202: index 2 into [$45]-[$4B] (use the [$47]/[$4B] positions)
$05:80BD C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$05:80BF 22 EC 88 05  JSL.L $88EC                     ; Build a Layer 1 tile column/row for this level mode ($88EC)
$05:80C3 22 55 89 05  JSL.L $8955                     ; Build the Layer 2 column/row for this level mode ($8955)
$05:80C7 22 AD 87 00  JSL.L $87AD                     ; DMA the built column to VRAM ($87AD)
$05:80CB C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$05:80CD E6 47        INC $47                         ; Next column/row position: [$47]++
$05:80CF E6 4B        INC $4B                         ; [$4B]++
$05:80D1 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:80D3 A5 47        LDA $47                         ; \
$05:80D5 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:80D6 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:80D7 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:80D8 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; |
$05:80DA 29 06 00     AND.W #$0006                    ; |
$05:80DD AA           TAX                             ; } X = ([$47] >> 3) & 6: cycling frame offset (4 frames, 2 bytes each)
$05:80DE A9 33 01     LDA.W #$0133                    ; \
$05:80E1 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:80E2 A8           TAY                             ; / Y = $133 * 2: entry of Map16 tile $133 in the pointer table at $0FBE
$05:80E3 A9 07 00     LDA.W #$0007                    ; \
$05:80E6 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = 7: loop counter (8 tiles, $133-$13A)
$05:80E8 BF 76 87 05  LDA.L MAP16AppTable,X           ; A = frame's base pointer from MAP16AppTable[X]
$05:80EC 99 BE 0F     STA.W $0FBE,Y                   ; Map16 tile pointer = A
$05:80EF C8           INY                             ; \
$05:80F0 C8           INY                             ; / Next table entry (Y += 2)
$05:80F1 18           CLC                             ; \
$05:80F2 69 08 00     ADC.W #$0008                    ; / Next tile's data is 8 bytes on
$05:80F5 C6 00        DEC $00                         ; \
$05:80F7 10 F3        BPL $80EC                       ; / Repeat for 8 tiles
$05:80F9 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:80FB EE 28 19     INC.W $1928                     ; [$1928]++
$05:80FE AD 28 19     LDA.W $1928                     ; \
$05:8101 C9 20        CMP.B #$20                      ; |
$05:8103 D0 B8        BNE $80BD                       ; / Loop until 32 columns/rows are drawn ([$1928] = $20)
$05:8105 AD 9D 0D     LDA.W $0D9D                     ; \
$05:8108 8D 2C 21     STA.W $212C                     ; } TM = [$0D9D] (layers on the main screen)
$05:810B 8D 2E 21     STA.W $212E                     ; / TMW = [$0D9D] (window mask for the main screen)
$05:810E AD 9E 0D     LDA.W $0D9E                     ; \
$05:8111 8D 2D 21     STA.W $212D                     ; } TS = [$0D9E] (layers on the subscreen)
$05:8114 8D 2F 21     STA.W $212F                     ; / TSW = [$0D9E] (window mask for the subscreen)
$05:8117 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8119 A9 FF FF     LDA.W #$FFFF                    ; \
$05:811C 85 4D        STA $4D                         ; |
$05:811E 85 4F        STA $4F                         ; |
$05:8120 85 51        STA $51                         ; } [$4D]-[$54] = $FFFF (reset the drawn-column markers)
$05:8122 85 53        STA $53                         ; /
$05:8124 28           PLP                             ; Restore processor flags
$05:8125 6B           RTL                             ; Return

$05:8126 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$05:8127 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$05:8129 A0 00 00     LDY.W #$0000                    ; \
$05:812C 84 03        STY $03                         ; |
$05:812E 84 05        STY $05                         ; / Y = 0; [$03] = 0 (source offset), [$05] = 0 (destination offset)
$05:8130 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:8132 A9 7E        LDA.B #$7E                      ; \
$05:8134 85 0F        STA $0F                         ; / [$0F] = $7E: destination bank
$05:8136 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8138 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; X and Y 16-bit
$05:813A A4 03        LDY $03                         ; Y = source offset [$03]
$05:813C B7 68        LDA [$68],Y                     ; \
$05:813E 85 07        STA $07                         ; / [$07] = next control byte from [$68]
$05:8140 C8           INY                             ; Y++
$05:8141 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8143 84 03        STY $03                         ; [$03] = Y
$05:8145 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8147 29 80        AND.B #$80                      ; \
$05:8149 F0 1F        BEQ $816A                       ; / Bit 7 set: RLE run; clear: literal copy
$05:814B A5 07        LDA $07                         ; \
$05:814D 29 7F        AND.B #$7F                      ; |
$05:814F 85 07        STA $07                         ; / [$07] = run length - 1 (control byte & $7F)
$05:8151 B7 68        LDA [$68],Y                     ; \
$05:8153 C8           INY                             ; / A = byte to repeat; Y++
$05:8154 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8156 84 03        STY $03                         ; [$03] = Y
$05:8158 A4 05        LDY $05                         ; Y = destination offset [$05]
$05:815A E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:815C 97 0D        STA [$0D],Y                     ; \
$05:815E C8           INY                             ; |
$05:815F C6 07        DEC $07                         ; |
$05:8161 10 F7        BPL $815A                       ; / Repeat until [$07] underflows
$05:8163 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8165 84 05        STY $05                         ; [$05] = Y (destination offset)
$05:8167 4C 88 81     JMP.W $8188                     ; Go check for the end marker

$05:816A C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:816C A4 03        LDY $03                         ; Y = source offset
$05:816E E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8170 B7 68        LDA [$68],Y                     ; \
$05:8172 C8           INY                             ; / Copy next literal byte from [$68],Y; Y++
$05:8173 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8175 84 03        STY $03                         ; [$03] = Y
$05:8177 A4 05        LDY $05                         ; Y = destination offset
$05:8179 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:817B 97 0D        STA [$0D],Y                     ; Store the byte at [$0D],Y
$05:817D C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:817F C8           INY                             ; Y++ (destination)
$05:8180 84 05        STY $05                         ; [$05] = Y
$05:8182 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8184 C6 07        DEC $07                         ; \
$05:8186 10 E2        BPL $816A                       ; / Repeat for [$07]+1 literal bytes
$05:8188 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:818A A4 03        LDY $03                         ; Y = source offset
$05:818C E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:818E B7 68        LDA [$68],Y                     ; \
$05:8190 C9 FF        CMP.B #$FF                      ; |
$05:8192 D0 A2        BNE $8136                       ; / If the next byte isn't $FF, read the next control byte
$05:8194 C8           INY                             ; Y++
$05:8195 B7 68        LDA [$68],Y                     ; \
$05:8197 C9 FF        CMP.B #$FF                      ; |
$05:8199 D0 9B        BNE $8136                       ; / Second byte must also be $FF, otherwise keep decoding
$05:819B C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:819D A9 00 91     LDA.W #$9100                    ; \
$05:81A0 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = $9100: base for the default Map16 pointer table
$05:81A2 A2 00 00     LDX.W #$0000                    ; X = 0
$05:81A5 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; A = [$00]
$05:81A7 9D BE 0F     STA.W $0FBE,X                   ; Pointer of Map16 tile X/2 = [$00]
$05:81AA A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$05:81AC 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:81AD 69 08 00     ADC.W #$0008                    ; |
$05:81B0 85 00        STA $00                         ; / Each tile's data is 8 bytes
$05:81B2 E8           INX                             ; \
$05:81B3 E8           INX                             ; / X += 2
$05:81B4 E0 00 04     CPX.W #$0400                    ; \
$05:81B7 D0 EC        BNE $81A5                       ; / Repeat for all 512 Map16 tiles (X = $400)
$05:81B9 28           PLP                             ; Restore processor flags
$05:81BA 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $81BB..81F3: Table: Map16 tile data source bitmask ;;;
;; 512 bits, one per Map16 tile ($000-$1FF), MSB first. Bit set: the tile's 8-byte data comes from the shared
;;     set at $05:8000;
;; clear: from the tileset-specific block. Read by $81FB.
$05:81BB              .db $FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF ; Map16 tiles $000-$03F: all from the shared set
$05:81C3              .db $FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$E0,$00 ; Tiles $040-$07F: $040-$06F and $070-$072 shared, rest tileset-specific
$05:81CB              .db $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Tiles $080-$0BF: all tileset-specific
$05:81D3              .db $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Tiles $0C0-$0FF: all tileset-specific
$05:81DB              .db $FE,$00,$7F,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF ; Tiles $100-$13F: mostly shared
$05:81E3              .db $FF,$FF,$E0,$00,$00,$03,$FF,$FF ; Tiles $140-$17F: mostly shared
$05:81EB              .db $FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF ; Tiles $180-$1BF: all shared
$05:81F3              .db $FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF,$FF ; Tiles $1C0-$1FF: all shared


;;; $81FB: Map16 tile pointers; level buffer fill routines ;;;
;; $0581FB: builds the 512-entry Map16 tile data pointer table at $0FBE using the bitmask above, tileset
;;     [$1931],
;; and sets [$1430]/[$1431] (probably the sprite-touchable tile range). For tilesets 0 and 7 it also disables
;;     that range and points tiles
;; $1C4-$1C7 and $1EC-$1EF at $8A70+.
;; $0582C8: stores A at X in each 512-byte page of $7EC800-$7EFFFF, then X++. $05833A: the same for
;;     $7FC800-$7FFFFF.
;; Parameters: A = value, X = offset within each page. Returns: X incremented.
;; Called by:
;;     $05:83B5: Load level header and tileset (LoadLevel)
$05:81FB E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:81FD AD 31 19     LDA.W $1931                     ; \
$05:8200 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8201 AA           TAX                             ; / X = tileset [$1931] * 2
$05:8202 A9 05        LDA.B #$05                      ; \
$05:8204 85 0F        STA $0F                         ; / [$0F] = $05: bank of the Map16 data
$05:8206 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$05:8208 85 84        STA $84                         ; / [$84] = 0 (purpose unclear)
$05:820A A9 C4        LDA.B #$C4                      ; \
$05:820C 8D 30 14     STA.W $1430                     ; / [$1430] = $C4: lower bound of the Map16 tile range sprites react to (probably)
$05:820F A9 CA        LDA.B #$CA                      ; \
$05:8211 8D 31 14     STA.W $1431                     ; / [$1431] = $CA: upper bound of that range (probably)
$05:8214 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8216 A9 5E E5     LDA.W #$E55E                    ; \
$05:8219 85 82        STA $82                         ; / [$82] = $E55E (pointer into bank $05 data, purpose unclear)
$05:821B BF 00 80 05  LDA.L TilesetMAP16Loc,X         ; \
$05:821F 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = pointer to this tileset's Map16 data (TilesetMAP16Loc[X])
$05:8221 A9 00 80     LDA.W #$8000                    ; \
$05:8224 85 02        STA $02                         ; / [$02] = $8000: start of the shared Map16 data
$05:8226 A9 BB 81     LDA.W #$81BB                    ; \
$05:8229 85 0D        STA $0D                         ; / [$0D] = $81BB: bitmask table (bank [$0F] = 5)
$05:822B 64 04        STZ $04                         ; \
$05:822D 64 09        STZ $09                         ; |
$05:822F 64 0B        STZ $0B                         ; / [$04] = [$09] = [$0B] = 0 ([$0B] = bit counter)
$05:8231 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; X and Y 16-bit
$05:8233 A0 00 00     LDY.W #$0000                    ; \
$05:8236 BB           TYX                             ; / Y = X = 0 (Y = bitmask byte, X = pointer table offset)
$05:8237 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8239 B7 0D        LDA [$0D],Y                     ; A = bitmask byte Y (one bit per Map16 tile)
$05:823B 85 0C        STA $0C                         ; [$0C] = bitmask byte
$05:823D 06 0C        ASL $0C                         ; Shift next bit into carry (1 = tile data comes from the shared set)
$05:823F 90 12        BCC $8253                       ; Bit clear: use the tileset-specific data
$05:8241 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8243 A5 02        LDA $02                         ; \
$05:8245 9D BE 0F     STA.W $0FBE,X                   ; / Tile pointer at $0FBE+X = [$02] (shared data)
$05:8248 A5 02        LDA $02                         ; \
$05:824A 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:824B 69 08 00     ADC.W #$0008                    ; |
$05:824E 85 02        STA $02                         ; / [$02] += 8 (each Map16 tile is 8 bytes)
$05:8250 4C 62 82     JMP.W $8262                     ; Next tile

$05:8253 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8255 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$05:8257 9D BE 0F     STA.W $0FBE,X                   ; / Tile pointer at $0FBE+X = [$00]
$05:825A A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$05:825C 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:825D 69 08 00     ADC.W #$0008                    ; |
$05:8260 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] += 8
$05:8262 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8264 E8           INX                             ; \
$05:8265 E8           INX                             ; / X += 2: next table entry
$05:8266 E6 09        INC $09                         ; [$09]++ (tile counter, apparently unused)
$05:8268 E6 0B        INC $0B                         ; Bit counter [$0B]++
$05:826A A5 0B        LDA $0B                         ; \
$05:826C C9 08        CMP.B #$08                      ; |
$05:826E D0 CD        BNE $823D                       ; / Repeat for the 8 bits of this byte
$05:8270 64 0B        STZ $0B                         ; [$0B] = 0
$05:8272 C8           INY                             ; Next bitmask byte
$05:8273 C0 40 00     CPY.W #$0040                    ; \
$05:8276 D0 BF        BNE $8237                       ; / Repeat for 64 bytes (512 Map16 tiles)
$05:8278 AD 31 19     LDA.W $1931                     ; \
$05:827B F0 04        BEQ $8281                       ; |
$05:827D C9 07        CMP.B #$07                      ; |
$05:827F D0 44        BNE $82C5                       ; / Only tilesets 0 and 7 continue; others return
$05:8281 A9 FF        LDA.B #$FF                      ; \
$05:8283 8D 30 14     STA.W $1430                     ; |
$05:8286 8D 31 14     STA.W $1431                     ; / [$1430] = [$1431] = $FF (empties the sprite-reactive tile range)
$05:8289 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$05:828B A9 C8 E5     LDA.W #$E5C8                    ; \
$05:828E 85 82        STA $82                         ; / [$82] = $E5C8 (alternate pointer for tilesets 0 and 7)
$05:8290 A9 C4 01     LDA.W #$01C4                    ; \
$05:8293 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8294 A8           TAY                             ; / Y = $1C4 * 2: pointer table entry of Map16 tile $1C4
$05:8295 A9 70 8A     LDA.W #$8A70                    ; \
$05:8298 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = $8A70: data for these tiles
$05:829A A2 03 00     LDX.W #$0003                    ; X = 3 (4 tiles)
$05:829D A5 00        LDA $00                         ; A = [$00]
$05:829F 99 BE 0F     STA.W $0FBE,Y                   ; Tile pointer = A
$05:82A2 18           CLC                             ; \
$05:82A3 69 08 00     ADC.W #$0008                    ; |
$05:82A6 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] += 8
$05:82A8 C8           INY                             ; \
$05:82A9 C8           INY                             ; / Y += 2
$05:82AA CA           DEX                             ; \
$05:82AB 10 F0        BPL $829D                       ; / Repeat for tiles $1C4-$1C7
$05:82AD A9 EC 01     LDA.W #$01EC                    ; \
$05:82B0 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:82B1 A8           TAY                             ; / Y = $1EC * 2: pointer table entry of Map16 tile $1EC
$05:82B2 A2 03 00     LDX.W #$0003                    ; X = 3 (4 tiles)
$05:82B5 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; A = [$00] (continues after $1C7's data)
$05:82B7 99 BE 0F     STA.W $0FBE,Y                   ; Tile pointer = A
$05:82BA 18           CLC                             ; \
$05:82BB 69 08 00     ADC.W #$0008                    ; |
$05:82BE 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] += 8
$05:82C0 C8           INY                             ; \
$05:82C1 C8           INY                             ; / Y += 2
$05:82C2 CA           DEX                             ; \
$05:82C3 10 F0        BPL $82B5                       ; / Repeat for tiles $1EC-$1EF
$05:82C5 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:82C7 60           RTS                             ; Return

$05:82C8 9F 00 C8 7E  STA.L $7EC800,X                 ; \
$05:82CC 9F 00 CA 7E  STA.L $7ECA00,X                 ; |
$05:82D0 9F 00 CC 7E  STA.L $7ECC00,X                 ; |
$05:82D4 9F 00 CE 7E  STA.L $7ECE00,X                 ; |
$05:82D8 9F 00 D0 7E  STA.L $7ED000,X                 ; |
$05:82DC 9F 00 D2 7E  STA.L $7ED200,X                 ; |
$05:82E0 9F 00 D4 7E  STA.L $7ED400,X                 ; |
$05:82E4 9F 00 D6 7E  STA.L $7ED600,X                 ; |
$05:82E8 9F 00 D8 7E  STA.L $7ED800,X                 ; |
$05:82EC 9F 00 DA 7E  STA.L $7EDA00,X                 ; |
$05:82F0 9F 00 DC 7E  STA.L $7EDC00,X                 ; |
$05:82F4 9F 00 DE 7E  STA.L $7EDE00,X                 ; |
$05:82F8 9F 00 E0 7E  STA.L $7EE000,X                 ; |
$05:82FC 9F 00 E2 7E  STA.L $7EE200,X                 ; } Store A at X within each of the 28 pages $7EC800-$7EFFFF (stride $200)
$05:8300 9F 00 E4 7E  STA.L $7EE400,X                 ; |
$05:8304 9F 00 E6 7E  STA.L $7EE600,X                 ; |
$05:8308 9F 00 E8 7E  STA.L $7EE800,X                 ; |
$05:830C 9F 00 EA 7E  STA.L $7EEA00,X                 ; |
$05:8310 9F 00 EC 7E  STA.L $7EEC00,X                 ; |
$05:8314 9F 00 EE 7E  STA.L $7EEE00,X                 ; |
$05:8318 9F 00 F0 7E  STA.L $7EF000,X                 ; |
$05:831C 9F 00 F2 7E  STA.L $7EF200,X                 ; |
$05:8320 9F 00 F4 7E  STA.L $7EF400,X                 ; |
$05:8324 9F 00 F6 7E  STA.L $7EF600,X                 ; |
$05:8328 9F 00 F8 7E  STA.L $7EF800,X                 ; |
$05:832C 9F 00 FA 7E  STA.L $7EFA00,X                 ; |
$05:8330 9F 00 FC 7E  STA.L $7EFC00,X                 ; |
$05:8334 9F 00 FE 7E  STA.L $7EFE00,X                 ; /
$05:8338 E8           INX                             ; X++ (next byte in each page)
$05:8339 60           RTS                             ; Return

$05:833A 9F 00 C8 7F  STA.L $7FC800,X                 ; \
$05:833E 9F 00 CA 7F  STA.L $7FCA00,X                 ; |
$05:8342 9F 00 CC 7F  STA.L $7FCC00,X                 ; |
$05:8346 9F 00 CE 7F  STA.L $7FCE00,X                 ; |
$05:834A 9F 00 D0 7F  STA.L $7FD000,X                 ; |
$05:834E 9F 00 D2 7F  STA.L $7FD200,X                 ; |
$05:8352 9F 00 D4 7F  STA.L $7FD400,X                 ; |
$05:8356 9F 00 D6 7F  STA.L $7FD600,X                 ; |
$05:835A 9F 00 D8 7F  STA.L $7FD800,X                 ; |
$05:835E 9F 00 DA 7F  STA.L $7FDA00,X                 ; |
$05:8362 9F 00 DC 7F  STA.L $7FDC00,X                 ; |
$05:8366 9F 00 DE 7F  STA.L $7FDE00,X                 ; |
$05:836A 9F 00 E0 7F  STA.L $7FE000,X                 ; |
$05:836E 9F 00 E2 7F  STA.L $7FE200,X                 ; } Store A at X within each of the 28 pages $7FC800-$7FFFFF (stride $200)
$05:8372 9F 00 E4 7F  STA.L $7FE400,X                 ; |
$05:8376 9F 00 E6 7F  STA.L $7FE600,X                 ; |
$05:837A 9F 00 E8 7F  STA.L $7FE800,X                 ; |
$05:837E 9F 00 EA 7F  STA.L $7FEA00,X                 ; |
$05:8382 9F 00 EC 7F  STA.L $7FEC00,X                 ; |
$05:8386 9F 00 EE 7F  STA.L $7FEE00,X                 ; |
$05:838A 9F 00 F0 7F  STA.L $7FF000,X                 ; |
$05:838E 9F 00 F2 7F  STA.L $7FF200,X                 ; |
$05:8392 9F 00 F4 7F  STA.L $7FF400,X                 ; |
$05:8396 9F 00 F6 7F  STA.L $7FF600,X                 ; |
$05:839A 9F 00 F8 7F  STA.L $7FF800,X                 ; |
$05:839E 9F 00 FA 7F  STA.L $7FFA00,X                 ; |
$05:83A2 9F 00 FC 7F  STA.L $7FFC00,X                 ; |
$05:83A6 9F 00 FE 7F  STA.L $7FFE00,X                 ; /
$05:83AA E8           INX                             ; X++ (next byte in each page)
$05:83AB 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $83AC: Load level header and tileset (LoadLevel) ;;;
;; Layer number [$1933] = 0, parses the level header at [$65] ($84E3) and sets up the tileset's Map16
;;     pointers ($81FB).
;; Called by:
;;     $05:808C: Level load: init buffers, background, start screens
$05:83AC 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$05:83AD E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:83AF 9C 33 19     STZ.W $1933                     ; Layer number [$1933] = 0 (layer 1)
$05:83B2 20 E3 84     JSR.W $84E3                     ; Parse the 5-byte level header ($84E3)
$05:83B5 20 FB 81     JSR.W $81FB                     ; Set up Map16 tile data pointers for the tileset ($81FB)

;;; $83B8: Load objects of one layer (LoadAgain) ;;;
;; Boss modes $09, $0B and $10 have no object data. Otherwise, if the layer's data does not start with $FF,
;;     loads its objects with LoadLevelData.
;; Reused for layer 2 (second pass with [$65] = [$68] + 5).
;; Called by:
;;     $05:840F: Switch to layer 2 objects or finish (LevLoadNotEmpty)
$05:83B8 AD 25 19     LDA.W $1925                     ; A = level mode [$1925]
$05:83BB C9 09        CMP.B #$09                      ; \
$05:83BD F0 53        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83BF C9 0B        CMP.B #$0B                      ; |
$05:83C1 F0 4F        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83C3 C9 10        CMP.B #$10                      ; |
$05:83C5 F0 4B        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; / Boss modes $09, $0B and $10 have no object data: finish
$05:83C7 A0 00        LDY.B #$00                      ; \
$05:83C9 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; |
$05:83CB C9 FF        CMP.B #$FF                      ; |
$05:83CD F0 03        BEQ LevLoadNotEmpty             ; / If the first object byte is $FF the level is empty: skip loading
$05:83CF 20 FF 85     JSR.W LoadLevelData             ; Load the layer's objects into the Map16 buffers (LoadLevelData)

;;; $83D2: Switch to layer 2 objects or finish (LevLoadNotEmpty) ;;;
;; Modes $00, $0A, $0C, $0D, $0E, $11 and $1E have no layer 2 objects. Otherwise bumps the layer number
;;     [$1933], points [$65]-[$67] at the
;; layer 2 object stream ([$68]-[$6A] + 5, past its header), clears [$1928] and loops back to LoadAgain.
;;     Finishes after layer 2.
$05:83D2 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:83D4 AD 25 19     LDA.W $1925                     ; A = level mode
$05:83D7 F0 39        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; \
$05:83D9 C9 0A        CMP.B #$0A                      ; |
$05:83DB F0 35        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83DD C9 0C        CMP.B #$0C                      ; |
$05:83DF F0 31        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83E1 C9 0D        CMP.B #$0D                      ; |
$05:83E3 F0 2D        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83E5 C9 0E        CMP.B #$0E                      ; |
$05:83E7 F0 29        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83E9 C9 11        CMP.B #$11                      ; |
$05:83EB F0 25        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; |
$05:83ED C9 1E        CMP.B #$1E                      ; |
$05:83EF F0 21        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; / Modes $00, $0A, $0C, $0D, $0E, $11 and $1E have no layer 2 objects: finish
$05:83F1 EE 33 19     INC.W $1933                     ; \
$05:83F4 AD 33 19     LDA.W $1933                     ; / Layer number [$1933]++ (to layer 2)
$05:83F7 C9 02        CMP.B #$02                      ; \
$05:83F9 F0 17        BEQ LoadLevelDone               ; / Both layers done: finish
$05:83FB A5 68        LDA $68                         ; \
$05:83FD 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:83FE 69 05        ADC.B #$05                      ; |
$05:8400 85 65        STA $65                         ; |
$05:8402 A5 69        LDA $69                         ; } [$65]-[$67] = [$68]-[$6A] + 5 (layer 2 data, skipping its 5-byte header)
$05:8404 69 00        ADC.B #$00                      ; |
$05:8406 85 66        STA $66                         ; |
$05:8408 A5 6A        LDA $6A                         ; |
$05:840A 85 67        STA $67                         ; /
$05:840C 9C 28 19     STZ.W $1928                     ; [$1928] = 0
$05:840F 4C B8 83     JMP.W LoadAgain                 ; Load the layer 2 objects


;;; $8412: Finish level load (LoadLevelDone) ;;;
;; Resets the layer number [$1933] to 0 and returns.
$05:8412 9C 33 19     STZ.W $1933                     ; Layer number [$1933] = 0
$05:8415 28           PLP                             ; Restore processor flags
$05:8416 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $8417: Table: level mode vertical flags (VerticalTable) ;;;
;; Indexed by level mode ($1925). Bit 0 = layer 1 is vertical, bit 1 = layer 2 is vertical; stored in [$5B].
;;     Bit 7 is set for some modes (meaning unclear).
$05:8417              .db $00,$00,$80,$01,$81,$02,$82,$03 ; Level modes $00-$07 (bit 0: vertical layer 1; bit 1: vertical layer 2)
$05:841F              .db $83,$00,$01,$00,$00,$01,$00,$00 ; Level modes $08-$0F
$05:8427              .db $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Level modes $10-$17
$05:842F              .db $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$80 ; Level modes $18-$1F

;;; $8437: Table: level mode main screen layers (LevMainScrnTbl) ;;;
;; TM value per level mode: bit 0 BG1, bit 1 BG2, bit 2 BG3, bit 4 OBJ. Stored in [$0D9D].
$05:8437              .db $15,$15,$17,$15,$15,$15,$17,$15 ; Level modes $00-$07 (bit 0 BG1, 1 BG2, 2 BG3, 4 OBJ)
$05:843F              .db $17,$15,$15,$15,$15,$15,$04,$04 ; Level modes $08-$0F
$05:8447              .db $15,$17,$15,$15,$15,$15,$15,$15 ; Level modes $10-$17
$05:844F              .db $15,$15,$15,$15,$15,$15,$01,$02 ; Level modes $18-$1F

;;; $8457: Table: level mode subscreen layers (LevSubScrnTbl) ;;;
;; TS value per level mode. Stored in [$0D9E].
$05:8457              .db $02,$02,$00,$02,$02,$02,$00,$02 ; Level modes $00-$07 (subscreen layers)
$05:845F              .db $00,$00,$02,$00,$02,$02,$13,$13 ; Level modes $08-$0F
$05:8467              .db $00,$00,$02,$02,$02,$02,$02,$02 ; Level modes $10-$17
$05:846F              .db $02,$02,$02,$02,$02,$02,$16,$15 ; Level modes $18-$1F

;;; $8477: Table: level mode color math settings (LevCGADSUBtable) ;;;
;; CGADSUB value per level mode. Stored in [$40].
$05:8477              .db $24,$24,$24,$24,$24,$24,$20,$24 ; Level modes $00-$07 (color math layers)
$05:847F              .db $24,$20,$24,$20,$70,$70,$24,$24 ; Level modes $08-$0F
$05:8487              .db $20,$FF,$24,$24,$24,$24,$24,$24 ; Level modes $10-$17
$05:848F              .db $24,$24,$24,$24,$24,$24,$21,$22 ; Level modes $18-$1F

;;; $8497: Table: level mode boss room type (SpecialLevTable) ;;;
;; Stored in [$0D9B]: $00 normal, $80 Iggy/Larry room, $C0 Morton/Ludwig/Roy room, $C1 Bowser. Bit 7 switches
;;     NMI/IRQ to the Mode 7 path.
$05:8497              .db $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Level modes $00-$07 (80/C0/C1 = boss room types)
$05:849F              .db $00,$C0,$00,$80,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Level modes $08-$0F: mode $09 = C0, mode $0B = 80
$05:84A7              .db $C1,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Level modes $10-$17: mode $10 = C1 (Bowser)
$05:84AF              .db $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; Level modes $18-$1F

;;; $84B7: Table: level mode sprite OAM property mask (LevXYPPCCCTtbl) ;;;
;; Stored in [$64]; XORed into most sprites' YXPPCCCT bytes (level modes using $20 vs $30).
$05:84B7              .db $20,$20,$20,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30 ; Level modes $00-$07 (sprite OAM property XOR mask)
$05:84BF              .db $30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$20,$20 ; Level modes $08-$0F
$05:84C7              .db $30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30 ; Level modes $10-$17
$05:84CF              .db $30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30,$30 ; Level modes $18-$1F

;;; $84D7: Table: level timer hundreds digit (TimerTable) ;;;
;; Indexed by header byte 4 bits 6-7: 0 = no timer, 2, 3 or 4 hundred seconds.
$05:84D7              .db $00,$02,$03,$04             ; Timer start (hundreds digit) for header values 0-3: 0, 2, 3, 4 (0 = no timer)


;;; $84DB: Music table; level header parse (bytes 1-2) (LevelMusicTable) ;;;
;; $0584DB: music track number for the 3-bit music field of the header.
;; $0584E3: parses the level header at [$65]. Byte 1: bits 0-4 screens - 1 ([$5D]), bits 5-7 BG palette
;;     ([$1930]).
;; Byte 2: bits 0-4 level mode ([$1925]), which indexes the mode tables for OAM mask, TM, TS, color math, boss
;;     type and vertical flags; bits 5-7 BG color ([$192F]).
;; Sets [$5E]/[$5F] (horizontal/vertical screen counts) from the screen count and vertical flag.
$05:84DB              .db $02,$06,$01,$08,$07,$03,$05,$12 ; Music track for header music values 0-7

$05:84E3 A0 00        LDY.B #$00                      ; Y = 0
$05:84E5 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; A = header byte 1
$05:84E7 AA           TAX                             ; Keep a copy in X
$05:84E8 29 1F        AND.B #$1F                      ; \
$05:84EA 1A           INC A                           ; |
$05:84EB 85 5D        STA RAM_ScreensInLvl            ; / Screens in level [$5D] = (byte1 & $1F) + 1
$05:84ED 8A           TXA                             ; \
$05:84EE 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:84EF 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:84F0 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:84F1 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:84F2 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:84F3 8D 30 19     STA.W $1930                     ; / [$1930] = byte1 >> 5 (BG palette)
$05:84F6 C8           INY                             ; \
$05:84F7 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; / A = header byte 2
$05:84F9 29 1F        AND.B #$1F                      ; \
$05:84FB 8D 25 19     STA.W $1925                     ; / Level mode [$1925] = byte2 & $1F
$05:84FE AA           TAX                             ; X = level mode
$05:84FF BF B7 84 05  LDA.L LevXYPPCCCTtbl,X          ; \
$05:8503 85 64        STA $64                         ; / [$64] = sprite OAM property XOR mask from LevXYPPCCCTtbl
$05:8505 BF 37 84 05  LDA.L LevMainScrnTbl,X          ; \
$05:8509 8D 9D 0D     STA.W $0D9D                     ; / TM mirror [$0D9D] = main screen layers from LevMainScrnTbl
$05:850C BF 57 84 05  LDA.L LevSubScrnTbl,X           ; \
$05:8510 8D 9E 0D     STA.W $0D9E                     ; / TS mirror [$0D9E] = subscreen layers from LevSubScrnTbl
$05:8513 BF 77 84 05  LDA.L LevCGADSUBtable,X         ; \
$05:8517 85 40        STA $40                         ; / [$40] = color math settings from LevCGADSUBtable
$05:8519 BF 97 84 05  LDA.L SpecialLevTable,X         ; \
$05:851D 8D 9B 0D     STA.W $0D9B                     ; / [$0D9B] = special level type from SpecialLevTable (80/C0/C1 = boss rooms)
$05:8520 BF 17 84 05  LDA.L VerticalTable,X           ; \
$05:8524 85 5B        STA RAM_IsVerticalLvl           ; / Vertical flags [$5B] from VerticalTable
$05:8526 4A           LSR                             ; Carry = bit 0 (vertical level)
$05:8527 A5 5D        LDA RAM_ScreensInLvl            ; A = screens in level
$05:8529 A2 01        LDX.B #$01                      ; X = 1
$05:852B 90 03        BCC LevelModeEven               ; Horizontal level: [$5E] = screens, [$5F] = 1
$05:852D AA           TAX                             ; \
$05:852E A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; / Vertical level: X = screens, A = 1

;;; $8530: Level header parse (bytes 2-5): music, timer, tileset (LevelModeEven) ;;;
;; Byte 3: sprite GFX set ([$192B]), music (into [$0DDA] with flags for 'same as before'), layer 3 priority
;;     (BGMODE mirror [$3E]).
;; Byte 4: timer (only if [$141A] = 0), FG palette ([$192D]), sprite palette ([$192E]).
;; Byte 5: tileset ([$1931]/[$1932]), item memory ([$13BE]), scroll mode ([$1412]; 3 also clears [$1411]).
$05:8530 85 5E        STA $5E                         ; [$5E] = horizontal screen count
$05:8532 86 5F        STX $5F                         ; [$5F] = vertical screen count
$05:8534 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; Reload header byte 2
$05:8536 4A           LSR                             ; \
$05:8537 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8538 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8539 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:853A 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:853B 8D 2F 19     STA.W $192F                     ; / [$192F] = byte2 >> 5 (BG color)
$05:853E C8           INY                             ; \
$05:853F B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; / A = header byte 3
$05:8541 85 00        STA $00                         ; [$00] = byte 3
$05:8543 AA           TAX                             ; X = byte 3
$05:8544 29 0F        AND.B #$0F                      ; \
$05:8546 8D 2B 19     STA.W $192B                     ; / Sprite GFX set [$192B] = byte3 & $0F
$05:8549 8A           TXA                             ; A = byte 3
$05:854A 4A           LSR                             ; \
$05:854B 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:854C 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:854D 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:854E 29 07        AND.B #$07                      ; |
$05:8550 AA           TAX                             ; / X = (byte3 >> 4) & 7: music index
$05:8551 BF DB 84 05  LDA.L LevelMusicTable,X         ; A = music track from LevelMusicTable
$05:8555 AE DA 0D     LDX.W $0DDA                     ; X = [$0DDA] (previous music value, sets N flag)
$05:8558 10 02        BPL $855C                       ; Bit 7 of [$0DDA] clear: skip
$05:855A 09 80        ORA.B #$80                      ; If [$0DDA] bit 7 was set, set bit 7 in the new value too
$05:855C CD DA 0D     CMP.W $0DDA                     ; Same track as [$0DDA]?
$05:855F D0 02        BNE $8563                       ; No: skip
$05:8561 09 40        ORA.B #$40                      ; Yes: set bit 6 (probably 'don't restart the music')
$05:8563 8D DA 0D     STA.W $0DDA                     ; [$0DDA] = new music value (with flags)
$05:8566 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$05:8568 29 80        AND.B #$80                      ; |
$05:856A 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:856B 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:856C 4A           LSR                             ; } [$3E] (BGMODE mirror) = 1, or 9 if byte3 bit 7 (layer 3 priority)
$05:856D 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:856E 09 01        ORA.B #$01                      ; |
$05:8570 85 3E        STA $3E                         ; /
$05:8572 C8           INY                             ; \
$05:8573 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; / A = header byte 4
$05:8575 85 00        STA $00                         ; [$00] = byte 4
$05:8577 4A           LSR                             ; \
$05:8578 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8579 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:857A 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:857B 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:857C 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:857D AA           TAX                             ; / X = byte4 >> 6 (timer setting)
$05:857E AD 1A 14     LDA.W $141A                     ; \
$05:8581 D0 0D        BNE $8590                       ; / [$141A] non-zero (e.g. level re-entered): keep the current timer
$05:8583 BF D7 84 05  LDA.L TimerTable,X              ; A = hundreds digit from TimerTable[X]
$05:8587 8D 31 0F     STA.W $0F31                     ; [$0F31] = hundreds digit
$05:858A 9C 32 0F     STZ.W $0F32                     ; [$0F32] = 0 (tens)
$05:858D 9C 33 0F     STZ.W $0F33                     ; [$0F33] = 0 (ones)
$05:8590 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; A = byte 4
$05:8592 29 07        AND.B #$07                      ; \
$05:8594 8D 2D 19     STA.W $192D                     ; / FG palette [$192D] = byte4 & 7
$05:8597 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; A = byte 4
$05:8599 29 38        AND.B #$38                      ; \
$05:859B 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:859C 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:859D 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:859E 8D 2E 19     STA.W $192E                     ; / Sprite palette [$192E] = (byte4 & $38) >> 3
$05:85A1 C8           INY                             ; \
$05:85A2 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; / A = header byte 5
$05:85A4 29 0F        AND.B #$0F                      ; \
$05:85A6 8D 31 19     STA.W $1931                     ; |
$05:85A9 8D 32 19     STA.W $1932                     ; / Tileset [$1931] and [$1932] = byte5 & $0F
$05:85AC B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; Reload byte 5
$05:85AE 29 C0        AND.B #$C0                      ; \
$05:85B0 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:85B1 2A           ROL                             ; |
$05:85B2 2A           ROL                             ; |
$05:85B3 8D BE 13     STA.W $13BE                     ; / Item memory setting [$13BE] = byte5 >> 6
$05:85B6 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; Reload byte 5
$05:85B8 29 30        AND.B #$30                      ; \
$05:85BA 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:85BB 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:85BC 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:85BD 4A           LSR                             ; / A = scroll setting (byte5 bits 4-5)
$05:85BE C9 03        CMP.B #$03                      ; \
$05:85C0 D0 05        BNE HeaderVHscroll              ; / Setting 3 = no scrolling: clear [$1411] and use 0
$05:85C2 9C 11 14     STZ.W $1411                     ; [$1411] = 0
$05:85C5 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; A = 0

;;; $85C7: Header scroll setting; swap object X/Y nibbles (HeaderVHscroll) ;;;
;; $0585C7: stores the scroll mode and advances [$65]-[$67] by 5 so it points at the object data. Returns.
;; $0585D8: for vertical layers, swaps the low nibbles of object bytes [$0A] and [$0B] (X and Y positions),
;;     except for screen exit/jump
;; extended objects ([$5A] = 0 and [$59] < 2).
$05:85C7 8D 12 14     STA.W $1412                     ; [$1412] = scroll setting
$05:85CA A5 65        LDA $65                         ; \
$05:85CC 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:85CD 69 05        ADC.B #$05                      ; |
$05:85CF 85 65        STA $65                         ; |
$05:85D1 A5 66        LDA $66                         ; |
$05:85D3 69 00        ADC.B #$00                      ; } Level object data follows the 5-byte header
$05:85D5 85 66        STA $66                         ; /
$05:85D7 60           RTS                             ; Return

$05:85D8 A5 5A        LDA $5A                         ; \
$05:85DA D0 06        BNE $85E2                       ; / [$5A] (object number) non-zero: swap the nibbles
$05:85DC A5 59        LDA $59                         ; A = [$59]
$05:85DE C9 02        CMP.B #$02                      ; \
$05:85E0 90 1C        BCC $85FE                       ; / Extended object [$59] < 2 (screen exit/jump): don't swap
$05:85E2 A5 0A        LDA $0A                         ; \
$05:85E4 29 0F        AND.B #$0F                      ; |
$05:85E6 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = low nibble of [$0A]
$05:85E8 A5 0B        LDA $0B                         ; \
$05:85EA 29 0F        AND.B #$0F                      ; |
$05:85EC 85 01        STA $01                         ; / [$01] = low nibble of [$0B]
$05:85EE A5 0A        LDA $0A                         ; \
$05:85F0 29 F0        AND.B #$F0                      ; |
$05:85F2 05 01        ORA $01                         ; |
$05:85F4 85 0A        STA $0A                         ; / [$0A] = high nibble of [$0A] | [$01]
$05:85F6 A5 0B        LDA $0B                         ; \
$05:85F8 29 F0        AND.B #$F0                      ; |
$05:85FA 05 00        ORA $00                         ; |
$05:85FC 85 0B        STA $0B                         ; / [$0B] = high nibble of [$0B] | [$00] (X/Y nibbles swapped)
$05:85FE 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $85FF: Load one level object and find its Map16 address (LoadLevelData) ;;;
;; Reads a 3-byte object at [$65] into [$0A], [$0B], [$59] and advances [$65]. Object number [$5A] = [$0B] >>
;;     4 | ([$0A] & $60) >> 1;
;; [$57] = YX position within the screen. Handles the new-screen flag ([$0A] bit 7 increments [$1928]), looks
;;     up the screen's Map16 low and
;; high byte buffer addresses via LoadBlkPtrs/LoadBlkTable2 into [$6B]-[$6D] and [$6E]-[$70] (+$100 if [$0A]
;;     bit 4 is set), then dispatches to the
;; extended or standard object loader.
;; Called by:
;;     $05:83CF: Load objects of one layer (LoadAgain)
;;     $05:86DF: Loop to next object (LevLoadContinue)
$05:85FF E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:8601 A0 00        LDY.B #$00                      ; \
$05:8603 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; |
$05:8605 85 0A        STA $0A                         ; |
$05:8607 C8           INY                             ; |
$05:8608 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; } Read 3 object bytes at [$65] into [$0A], [$0B], [$59]
$05:860A 85 0B        STA $0B                         ; |
$05:860C C8           INY                             ; |
$05:860D B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; |
$05:860F 85 59        STA $59                         ; /
$05:8611 C8           INY                             ; \
$05:8612 98           TYA                             ; |
$05:8613 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:8614 65 65        ADC $65                         ; |
$05:8616 85 65        STA $65                         ; } [$65]-[$67] += 3 (bytes consumed)
$05:8618 A5 66        LDA $66                         ; |
$05:861A 69 00        ADC.B #$00                      ; |
$05:861C 85 66        STA $66                         ; /
$05:861E A5 0B        LDA $0B                         ; \
$05:8620 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8621 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8622 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8623 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:8624 85 5A        STA $5A                         ; } [$5A] = object number: [$0B] >> 4 | ([$0A] & $60) >> 1
$05:8626 A5 0A        LDA $0A                         ; |
$05:8628 29 60        AND.B #$60                      ; |
$05:862A 4A           LSR                             ; |
$05:862B 05 5A        ORA $5A                         ; |
$05:862D 85 5A        STA $5A                         ; /
$05:862F A5 5B        LDA RAM_IsVerticalLvl           ; A = vertical flags [$5B]
$05:8631 AC 33 19     LDY.W $1933                     ; \
$05:8634 F0 01        BEQ $8637                       ; |
$05:8636 4A           LSR                             ; / Layer 1 uses bit 0 of [$5B] (vertical level); layer 2 shifts to use bit 1
$05:8637 29 01        AND.B #$01                      ; \
$05:8639 F0 03        BEQ $863E                       ; / If this layer is vertical, swap the object's X/Y nibbles first
$05:863B 20 D8 85     JSR.W $85D8                     ; Swap object X/Y nibbles for vertical levels ($85D8)
$05:863E A5 0A        LDA $0A                         ; \
$05:8640 29 0F        AND.B #$0F                      ; |
$05:8642 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8643 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8644 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8645 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8646 85 57        STA $57                         ; } [$57] high nibble = Y position ([$0A] & $0F)
$05:8648 A5 0B        LDA $0B                         ; \
$05:864A 29 0F        AND.B #$0F                      ; |
$05:864C 05 57        ORA $57                         ; |
$05:864E 85 57        STA $57                         ; / [$57] |= X position ([$0B] & $0F): [$57] = YX within the screen
$05:8650 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8652 AD 33 19     LDA.W $1933                     ; \
$05:8655 29 FF 00     AND.W #$00FF                    ; |
$05:8658 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8659 AA           TAX                             ; / X = layer number * 2
$05:865A BF A8 BE 00  LDA.L LoadBlkPtrs,X             ; A = LoadBlkPtrs[layer]: table of low-byte screen address tables
$05:865E 85 03        STA $03                         ; [$03] = pointer (bank 0)
$05:8660 BF AC BE 00  LDA.L LoadBlkTable2,X           ; A = LoadBlkTable2[layer]: table for high bytes
$05:8664 85 06        STA $06                         ; [$06] = pointer (bank 0)
$05:8666 AD 25 19     LDA.W $1925                     ; \
$05:8669 29 1F 00     AND.W #$001F                    ; |
$05:866C 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:866D A8           TAY                             ; / Y = level mode * 2
$05:866E E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8670 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$05:8672 85 05        STA $05                         ; |
$05:8674 85 08        STA $08                         ; / [$05] = [$08] = 0 (bank bytes)
$05:8676 B7 03        LDA [$03],Y                     ; \
$05:8678 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = low byte of the screen address table for this level mode
$05:867A B7 06        LDA [$06],Y                     ; \
$05:867C 85 0D        STA $0D                         ; / [$0D] = low byte of the high-byte table address
$05:867E C8           INY                             ; Y++
$05:867F B7 03        LDA [$03],Y                     ; \
$05:8681 85 01        STA $01                         ; / [$01] = high byte
$05:8683 B7 06        LDA [$06],Y                     ; \
$05:8685 85 0E        STA $0E                         ; / [$0E] = high byte
$05:8687 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$05:8689 85 02        STA $02                         ; |
$05:868B 85 0F        STA $0F                         ; / [$02] = [$0F] = 0 (bank bytes)
$05:868D A5 0A        LDA $0A                         ; \
$05:868F 29 80        AND.B #$80                      ; |
$05:8691 0A           ASL                             ; |
$05:8692 6D 28 19     ADC.W $1928                     ; |
$05:8695 8D 28 19     STA.W $1928                     ; } New page flag ([$0A] bit 7): [$1928]++ (A = screen number)
$05:8698 8D A1 1B     STA.W $1BA1                     ; [$1BA1] = current screen number
$05:869B 0A           ASL                             ; \
$05:869C 18           CLC                             ; |
$05:869D 6D 28 19     ADC.W $1928                     ; |
$05:86A0 A8           TAY                             ; / Y = screen number * 3 (3-byte pointer per screen)
$05:86A1 B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; \
$05:86A3 85 6B        STA $6B                         ; / [$6B] = low byte of this screen's start in the Map16 low-byte buffer (table [$00])
$05:86A5 B7 0D        LDA [$0D],Y                     ; \
$05:86A7 85 6E        STA $6E                         ; / [$6E] = same for the Map16 high-byte buffer (table [$0D])
$05:86A9 C8           INY                             ; Y++
$05:86AA B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; \
$05:86AC 85 6C        STA $6C                         ; / [$6C] = middle byte of the low-byte buffer address
$05:86AE B7 0D        LDA [$0D],Y                     ; \
$05:86B0 85 6F        STA $6F                         ; / [$6F] = middle byte of the high-byte buffer address
$05:86B2 C8           INY                             ; Y++
$05:86B3 B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; \
$05:86B5 85 6D        STA $6D                         ; / [$6D] = bank of the low-byte buffer address (expected $7E)
$05:86B7 B7 0D        LDA [$0D],Y                     ; \
$05:86B9 85 70        STA $70                         ; / [$70] = bank of the high-byte buffer address (expected $7F)
$05:86BB A5 0A        LDA $0A                         ; \
$05:86BD 29 10        AND.B #$10                      ; |
$05:86BF F0 04        BEQ LoadNoHiCoord               ; / Object's high coordinate bit ([$0A] bit 4) set?
$05:86C1 E6 6C        INC $6C                         ; \
$05:86C3 E6 6F        INC $6F                         ; / Yes: [$6C]++ and [$6F]++ (second half of the screen buffer: lower half of horizontal levels, right half of vertical ones)

;;; $86C5: Dispatch to extended or standard object (LoadNoHiCoord) ;;;
;; Object number 0 means an extended object ($A100); otherwise the standard object loader runs.
$05:86C5 A5 5A        LDA $5A                         ; \
$05:86C7 D0 06        BNE LevLoadJsrNrm               ; / [$5A] = object number; non-zero is a standard object
$05:86C9 20 E3 86     JSR.W LevLoadExtObj             ; Object number 0: load an extended object
$05:86CC 4C D2 86     JMP.W LevLoadContinue           ; Continue (a BRA would have done)


;;; $86CF: Call standard object loader (LevLoadJsrNrm) ;;;
;; Calls LevLoadNrmObj ($05:86EA).
$05:86CF 20 EA 86     JSR.W LevLoadNrmObj             ; Load a standard object (LevLoadNrmObj)

;;; $86D2: Loop to next object (LevLoadContinue) ;;;
;; If the next byte at [$65] is not $FF, loads the next object, otherwise returns.
;; Called by:
;;     $05:86CC: Dispatch to extended or standard object (LoadNoHiCoord)
$05:86D2 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:86D4 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; X and Y 16-bit
$05:86D6 A0 00 00     LDY.W #$0000                    ; \
$05:86D9 B7 65        LDA [$65],Y                     ; |
$05:86DB C9 FF        CMP.B #$FF                      ; |
$05:86DD F0 03        BEQ LevelDataEnd                ; / Next byte at [$65] = $FF ends the layer's object list
$05:86DF 4C FF 85     JMP.W LoadLevelData             ; Otherwise load the next object


;;; $86E2: Return: object list finished (LevelDataEnd) ;;;
$05:86E2 60           RTS                             ; Return: all objects loaded


;;; $86E3: Load extended object (LevLoadExtObj) ;;;
;; Calls $A100 in bank $0D to load an extended object.
;; Called by:
;;     $05:86C9: Dispatch to extended or standard object (LoadNoHiCoord)
$05:86E3 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:86E5 22 00 A1 0D  JSL.L $A100                     ; Run the extended object handler ($A100)
$05:86E9 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $86EA: Layer scroll tile loader (check boundaries) (LevLoadNrmObj) ;;;
;; $0586EA: loads one normal level object via $A40F (companion of LevLoadExtObj at $0586E3).
;; $0586F1: called every frame from the level game mode after scrolling. For layer 1 and layer 2 it compares
;;     the 16-pixel-aligned scroll
;; position with the last loaded position ([$4D]-[$50] for layer 1, [$51]-[$54] for layer 2, indexed by scroll
;;     direction [$55]/[$56]).
;; On a change it stores the new position, sets the other direction's slot to $FFFF and calls the column/row
;;     loader for the level mode.
;; Bit 0 / bit 1 of [RAM_IsVerticalLvl] select position X (horizontal) or Y (vertical) for layer 1 / layer 2.
;; Called by:
;;     $05:86CF: Call standard object loader (LevLoadJsrNrm)
$05:86EA E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$05:86EC 22 0F A4 0D  JSL.L $A40F                     ; Load a normal (non-extended) level object ($A40F)
$05:86F0 60           RTS                             ; Return

$05:86F1 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$05:86F2 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$05:86F4 20 7E 87     JSR.W $877E                     ; Compute tile range bounds [$45]-[$4B] and the Map16 pointer table ($877E)
$05:86F7 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:86F9 A5 5B        LDA RAM_IsVerticalLvl           ; \
$05:86FB 29 01        AND.B #$01                      ; |
$05:86FD D0 14        BNE $8713                       ; / Layer 1 vertical (bit 0 of [$5B] set)? Then go to $058713
$05:86FF C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8701 A5 55        LDA $55                         ; \
$05:8703 29 FF 00     AND.W #$00FF                    ; |
$05:8706 AA           TAX                             ; } X = [$55] (layer 1 scroll direction index, 0 or 2)
$05:8707 A5 1A        LDA RAM_ScreenBndryXLo          ; \
$05:8709 29 F0 FF     AND.W #$FFF0                    ; / A = screen X position rounded down to a multiple of 16
$05:870C D5 4D        CMP $4D,X                       ; Same 16-pixel column as last loaded ([$4D,X])?
$05:870E F0 27        BEQ $8737                       ; Yes: layer 1 is up to date, go check layer 2 ($058737)
$05:8710 4C 24 87     JMP.W $8724                     ; No: go load a new column ($058724)

$05:8713 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8715 A5 55        LDA $55                         ; \
$05:8717 29 FF 00     AND.W #$00FF                    ; |
$05:871A AA           TAX                             ; } X = [$55] (layer 1 scroll direction index, 0 or 2)
$05:871B A5 1C        LDA RAM_ScreenBndryYLo          ; \
$05:871D 29 F0 FF     AND.W #$FFF0                    ; / A = screen Y position rounded down to a multiple of 16
$05:8720 D5 4D        CMP $4D,X                       ; Same 16-pixel row as last loaded ([$4D,X])?
$05:8722 F0 13        BEQ $8737                       ; Yes: layer 1 is up to date, go check layer 2 ($058737)
$05:8724 95 4D        STA $4D,X                       ; Remember this boundary as the last loaded position [$4D,X]
$05:8726 8A           TXA                             ; \
$05:8727 49 02 00     EOR.W #$0002                    ; |
$05:872A AA           TAX                             ; } X ^= 2: the other direction slot
$05:872B A9 FF FF     LDA.W #$FFFF                    ; \
$05:872E 95 4D        STA $4D,X                       ; / Invalidate the other slot: [$4D,X] = $FFFF (forces a reload if the scroll reverses)
$05:8730 22 1A 88 05  JSL.L $881A                     ; Load the layer 1 column/row ($881A, by level mode [$1925])
$05:8734 4C 74 87     JMP.W $8774                     ; Skip layer 2, restore flags and return ($058774)

$05:8737 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8739 A5 5B        LDA RAM_IsVerticalLvl           ; \
$05:873B 29 02        AND.B #$02                      ; |
$05:873D D0 14        BNE $8753                       ; / Layer 2 vertical (bit 1 of [$5B] set)? Then go to $058753
$05:873F C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8741 A5 56        LDA $56                         ; \
$05:8743 29 FF 00     AND.W #$00FF                    ; |
$05:8746 AA           TAX                             ; } X = [$56] (layer 2 scroll direction index, 0 or 2)
$05:8747 A5 1E        LDA $1E                         ; \
$05:8749 29 F0 FF     AND.W #$FFF0                    ; / A = layer 2 X position ($1E) rounded down to a multiple of 16
$05:874C D5 51        CMP $51,X                       ; Same 16-pixel column as last loaded ([$51,X])?
$05:874E F0 24        BEQ $8774                       ; Yes: nothing to load, return
$05:8750 4C 64 87     JMP.W $8764                     ; No: go load a new layer 2 column ($058764)

$05:8753 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8755 A5 56        LDA $56                         ; \
$05:8757 29 FF 00     AND.W #$00FF                    ; |

$05:875D 29 F0 FF     AND.W #$FFF0                    ; / A = layer 2 Y position ($20) rounded down to a multiple of 16
$05:8760 D5 51        CMP $51,X                       ; Same 16-pixel row as last loaded ([$51,X])?
$05:8762 F0 10        BEQ $8774                       ; Yes: nothing to load, return
$05:8764 95 51        STA $51,X                       ; Remember this boundary as the last loaded position [$51,X]
$05:8766 8A           TXA                             ; \
$05:8767 49 02 00     EOR.W #$0002                    ; |

$05:876B A9 FF FF     LDA.W #$FFFF                    ; \

;;; $8776: Map16 pointer bases and tile range setup (MAP16AppTable) ;;;
;; $058776: four 16-bit pointer bases ($8AB0, $84E0, $8AF0, $8B30) used to seed the Map16 pointer table at
;;     $0FBE.
;; $05877E: computes the range of tile columns (or rows) to keep loaded around the screen: [$45] = start - 8
;;     and [$47] = start + $17 for layer 1,
;; [$49]/[$4B] likewise for layer 2. For horizontal layer 1 it also fills 8 words at $1224 with the base
;;     chosen by the column group, step 8.
;; The Map16 pointer table use is inferred, hedged. Also contains $881A, the start of the layer 1 loader
;;     dispatch (level mode [$1925]).
$05:8776              .db $B0,$8A,$E0,$84,$F0,$8A,$30,$8B ; Map16 pointer bases $8AB0, $84E0, $8AF0, $8B30 (indexed by scroll column bits 4-5)

$05:877E 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$05:877F E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$05:8781 A5 5B        LDA RAM_IsVerticalLvl           ; \
$05:8783 29 01        AND.B #$01                      ; |
$05:8785 D0 44        BNE $87CB                       ; / Layer 1 vertical (bit 0 of [$5B] set)? Then go to $0587CB
$05:8787 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$05:8789 A5 1A        LDA RAM_ScreenBndryXLo          ; A = screen X position of layer 1
$05:878B 4A           LSR                             ; \

$05:8794 85 45        STA $45                         ; [$45] = left edge of the tile range (column - 8)
$05:8796 98           TYA                             ; A = tile column
$05:8797 18           CLC                             ; \

;;; $895E: Layer 2 update table and stripe builders (PtrsLong05895E) ;;;
;; Pointer table of 3-byte long pointers ($8955 dispatches through it with ExecutePtrLong), indexed by
;;     level mode [$1925] (0-$1F).
;; Followed by the routines it points to. Each builds one stripe of 8x8 tile words in the layer 2 VRAM update
;;     buffers at $1CE6-$1D6B:
;; VRAM address in $1CE6/$1CE7, then two tile words per 16x16 Map16 block, for the layer 2 block position
;;     [$49+[$56]].
;; $8B8D (modes 1-4, horizontal levels): one column of 27 blocks into $1CE8/$1CEA/$1D68/$1D6A.
;; $8C71 (modes 5-8, vertical levels): one row of 32 blocks into $1CE8 (top) and $1D68 (bottom).
;; $8D7A (mode 0 and others, prebuilt background): column read from the Map16 copy at $7E:B900/$7E:BD00,
;;     using $1928.
;; Both level-mode routines OR [$03] = $1000 into every tile word when tileset [$1931] = 3 (palette bit 2).
;; Layer 1 uses near-identical routines at $89CE (column) and $8A9B (row) with buffers at
;;     $1BE4-$1D65.
;; Note: LEVEL_PIPELINE_NOTES.md labels the 0588EC/058955 pair layer 2/layer 3; the RAM use ($45 vs $49, $1BE4
;;     vs $1CE6) points to layer 1/layer 2.
$05:895E 7A 8D 05     .dw $8D7A .db :$CODE_058D7A     ; Mode $00 - layer 2 update from prebuilt background ($7E:B900)
$05:8961 8D 8B 05     .dw $8B8D .db :$CODE_058B8D     ; Mode $01 - layer 2 column update (horizontal scroll)
$05:8964 8D 8B 05     .dw $8B8D .db :$CODE_058B8D     ; Mode $02 - layer 2 column update (horizontal scroll)
$05:8967 8D 8B 05     .dw $8B8D .db :$CODE_058B8D     ; Mode $03 - layer 2 column update (horizontal scroll)
$05:896A 8D 8B 05     .dw $8B8D .db :$CODE_058B8D     ; Mode $04 - layer 2 column update (horizontal scroll)
$05:896D 71 8C 05     .dw $8C71 .db :$CODE_058C71     ; Mode $05 - layer 2 row update (vertical scroll)
$05:8970 71 8C 05     .dw $8C71 .db :$CODE_058C71     ; Mode $06 - layer 2 row update (vertical scroll)
$05:8973 71 8C 05     .dw $8C71 .db :$CODE_058C71     ; Mode $07 - layer 2 row update (vertical scroll)

;;; $9000: Layer 3 images, message box text and routine (Layer3Ptr) ;;;
;; $059000 Layer3Ptr: 45 three-byte pointers to Layer 3 (BG3) stripe images, 3 per tileset; index = 3 *
;;     [$1931] + [$1BE3] - 1 (see $00A02F). Most point at $059549.
;; $059087-$05A57F: the stripe images, loaded with $871E. Record: VRAM address hi, lo; byte 3: bit 7
;;     vertical, bit 6 RLE, low 6 bits = length hi; length lo
;;   (bytes - 1); then tile/attribute pairs (RLE: one pair, repeated). A first byte with bit 7 set ends the
;;       image. Purpose of each image not verified.
;; $05A580-$05B0FE: message box data: text row VRAM addresses, level-to-message table, message text offsets,
;;     and the text. Text codes: A-Z = $00-$19, a-z = $40-$59,
;;   $1A ! , $1B . , $1D , , $1E ? , $1F space, $5D apostrophe; bit 7 = last character of the 18-tile row
;;       (rest of the row is blank).
;; $05B0FF: stripe image $09 (blank fill that erases the text box). $05B106-$05B10B: three 2-entry tables for
;;     the box animation.
;; $05B10C: message box routine, called by InLevelGameMode ($00A1DF) while [$1426] != 0. State [$1B88] = 0:
;;     window grows (+4 per frame in [$1B89], max $50),
;;   at $4C the text is built; press a button to close ([$1B88] = 1: shrinks, text erased at $50). In the
;;       intro level or a Switch Palace it ends the level.
;; Quirk: this section ends at $05B15D, in the middle of the routine; the rest (SubSideExit..) continues in
;;     the next section.
